title: Jude and the Terminal
premise: Rosalind Winterbourne, a veteran terraformer hauling cargo through contested orbits, is summoned when the deep-space vessel Halcyon returns with its crew mysteriously aged backward and no memory of their voyage. Digging into the ship's corrupted logs, she uncovers evidence of a massacre at a research station — evidence that every official record has been erased to protect a powerful orbital consortium. As she races to restore the truth, Rosalind falls for Jude, a de-aged crew member whose recovered memories hold the key, forcing her to choose between the man she loves and the duty that demands she expose him as both victim and unwitting accomplice. In the end, Rosalind broadcasts the restored records from the terraforming garden itself, sacrificing her career and nearly her life, while Jude — choosing truth over the comfortable lie of his rewritten past — stands beside her as the consortium begins to fall.
about_author: Juniper Vane is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing technical manuals before turning to fiction about the people who keep the solar system running. She writes from a converted shipping container studio overlooking a launch corridor, where she collects decommissioned flight recorders.

chapters.title: The Garden for the Unborn
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She tends the seed vaults of Meridian Station, a garden designed for colonists not yet conceived, while hauling cargo runs through increasingly hostile orbits. The chapter establishes her loneliness, her fifteen years of service, and her quiet pride in work no one will thank her for. Emotional beat: devoted isolation.

chapters.title: A Ship That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The long-lost Halcyon drifts into contested space, broadcasting an ancient distress code. Docking crews find thirty-one crew members biologically aged backward — some now children, all missing the memories of their voyage. Rosalind, nearest qualified responder, is ordered aboard. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in wonder.

chapters.title: Thirty-One Strangers
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She catalogs the de-aged crew and meets Jude Okonkwo, physically twenty but carrying fragments of a life he can't place. He recognizes her name from something he can't remember reading. Official observers arrive and begin sealing the ship. Emotional beat: uneasy connection amid institutional suspicion.

chapters.title: Records of Nothing
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Interrogated gently by consortium liaison Director Hale, Jude realizes his own logs have been scrubbed — not deleted, overwritten with plausible fabrications. He remembers fire, screaming, a station called Perdita, and nothing else. He lies to Hale about what he recalls. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: Perdita
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Cross-referencing old cargo manifests, Rosalind finds that Perdita Station existed — and then didn't; every database shows it never was. Her own delivery records from nine years ago are gone too. Someone with root access across the whole network erased a place. Emotional beat: vertigo of gaslighting.

chapters.title: What the Body Remembers
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Medical scans show the de-aging wasn't random: it's a side effect of experimental temporal shielding deployed during an emergency. Jude's muscle memory betrays him — he can operate weapons systems he's never been trained on. He starts secretly meeting Rosalind to compare fragments. Emotional beat: intimacy built on shared brokenness.

chapters.title: Hale's Kind Offer
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Director Hale offers Rosalind a promotion and permanent posting if she signs off on the official finding: the Halcyon suffered an accident, no station involved. She recognizes the bribe for what it is — confirmation there's something to bury. Emotional beat: temptation measured against conscience.

chapters.title: The Child Who Was the Captain
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The Halcyon's captain, now eight years old, draws the station's layout from memory — including decks that match no blueprint. A child's drawing becomes the first physical corroboration. Jude realizes the massacre happened during an evacuation the crew was forced to block. Emotional beat: horror through innocence.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rival factions maneuver over custody of the Halcyon; Rosalind's cargo routes are revoked, stranding her assets. She learns the consortium plans to move the crew to a 'rehabilitation facility' — effectively disappearing them. Emotional beat: the machinery closing in.

chapters.title: Fragments in the Dark
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Under sedation-free hypnosis, Jude recovers a full memory: Perdita's researchers begging for evacuation, orders from above to maintain silence, the shield overload that killed hundreds and rewound the survivors. He wakes sobbing Rosalind's name — she appears in the memory, delivering supplies that day. Emotional beat: devastating recognition.

chapters.title: You Were There
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Confronted with Jude's memory, Rosalind excavates her own past: she signed a manifest at Perdita, was paid to forget, took the hush money without knowing what it bought. Guilt reframes her fifteen years of dutiful service. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude discovers his pre-voyage self helped design the temporal shields used in the cover-up — he isn't only a victim but an architect. He considers accepting Hale's quiet deal: restoration treatment in exchange for silence. Emotional beat: identity cracking under complicity.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Garden
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind realizes Meridian's seed vault runs on isolated, air-gapped hardware — the one system the erasure couldn't reach. Old backups, including her Perdita manifests, may survive in cold storage. But reaching them means breaking station law. Emotional beat: hope found in obsolete things.

chapters.title: Cold Storage
chapters.summary: Dual POV. During a scheduled power-down, Rosalind and Jude infiltrate the vault levels together. They recover partial Perdita records — casualty lists, Jude's own signature on the shield specs — but trip a silent alarm. Emotional beat: tenderness and terror in equal measure.

chapters.title: Sealed
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Hale locks down Meridian, branding Rosalind a saboteur. Her crew abandons her; her access is stripped. Jude is taken for 'treatment.' Alone in the garden she built for the unborn, she decides the records broadcast from here or nowhere. Emotional beat: abandonment crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: The Treatment
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In the facility, Jude undergoes memory 'restoration' — actually a second overwrite. Fighting the process, he hides a data shard containing the recovered massacre memory inside his medical implant. He escapes during transfer, half-erased, running on instinct toward Meridian. Emotional beat: selfhood defended by a thread.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind rallies the de-aged crew, hiding aboard Meridian, arguing they are witnesses, not wreckage. The child-captain gives formal testimony. They plan to hijack the station's terraforming broadcast array — built to reach every colony — to transmit the archive. Emotional beat: the discarded becoming the decisive.

chapters.title: Countermeasures
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Wounded and partially memory-wiped, Jude reaches Meridian but doesn't remember Rosalind — only the shard and a feeling. She must decide whether to trust a man who may be Hale's Trojan horse. His implant data proves genuine. Emotional beat: love tested by erasure, chosen anyway.

chapters.title: Broadcast Day
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The crew seizes the broadcast array as Hale's security storms the garden. Rosalind uploads the Perdita archive — casualty lists, forged logs, Jude's testimony — to every colony channel in the system. Security breaches the vault; she stays at the console until transmission completes. Emotional beat: sacrifice in real time.

chapters.title: The Truth at Light-Speed
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Across the colonies, the massacre goes public. Colonies suspend consortium contracts; Hale's allies defect; an independent tribunal convenes. On Meridian, Rosalind is arrested — but the war is already lost for the conspirators. Jude testifies despite his fragmented mind. Emotional beat: vindication arriving too late to feel like victory.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Name
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Months later, Perdita Station is officially re-entered into the record; the dead are named. Jude chooses not to undergo full restoration, keeping his broken memories rather than risk losing what he's built since. He and Rosalind plant the first seeds from the vault in open ground. Emotional beat: grief integrated, identity self-authored.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The tribunal dissolves the consortium's charter; Rosalind, pardoned, declines reinstatement and instead takes charge of Meridian's garden, now renamed for Perdita's dead. Jude stays. The garden meant for the unborn finally has a present-tense purpose. Final beat: love and truth, both survived, taking root.
